subject: POC kickoff & hands-on session — schedule + sample payloads
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Morgan Blake <morgan.blake@quickcommerce.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 17:08:00 -0700
Subject: POC kickoff & hands-on session — schedule + sample payloads

Hi Morgan —

Thanks again for the time last week. We’re ready to run the hands-on portion of the POC where we’ll:
- walk through prompt sets and routing rules
- exercise load tests against a sample traffic profile
- validate redaction and KV/prefix caching behavior on your payload shapes

Proposed kickoff: Wed, May 20, 10:00–11:30 PT. That session would be a combined demo + working session (Marissa will drive the prompt review and test plan).

Action items for QuickCommerce before the session:
1) Share representative sample payloads (transactions, search queries, user chat snippets). If any values are PHI/PII please redact before sharing.
2) A short list (10–20) of priority prompts/evaluation sets you want us to run.
3) Any routing rules or labels you currently use in-prod (e.g., "priority_checkout", "ab_test_groupA").

We can accept a redacted JSON file or a CSV for simpler payloads. You can upload to the Drive link below or email attachments.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1QCb-example-drive-link

If Wed 10am PT doesn’t work, suggest two alternatives and we’ll adapt.

Thanks —
Rishi
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0127

From: Morgan Blake <morgan.blake@quickcommerce.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Torres <sam.torres@quickcommerce.com>, legal@quickcommerce.com
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 09:42:00 -0400
Subject: Re: POC kickoff & hands-on session — schedule + sample payloads

Thanks, Rishi — Wed 10am PT works for most of our team. Quick answers and attachments below.

We uploaded a first-pass of sample payloads to your Drive folder (file: quickcommerce_sample_payloads_v1.json). Note: several fields still contain order_ids and email fragments we’d prefer redacted. Our security team suggested we remove exact email addresses and full credit-card PANs.

Attached here: quickcommerce_sample_payloads_v1.json (Drive) — we can produce a sanitized redacted export by end of day Thursday.

Priority prompts we want covered:
- checkout_failure_explain (how to surface next-best actions for failed card auth)
- upsell_product_suggestions (given recent cart + behavior)
- search_rewrite_autocomplete (short queries that need expansion)

Routing rules: we have three labels in prod: priority_checkout, promo_candidate, and low_confidence.

One question: for load testing, what’s a safe per-minute TPS/multi-user model that won’t trigger infra throttles on your hosted tier?

Best,
Morgan
Product Ops, QuickCommerce

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Morgan Blake <morgan.blake@quickcommerce.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC kickoff & hands-on session — schedule + sample payloads

Appreciate the upload, Morgan — that’s perfect as a starting point. A couple of notes:

1) Please go ahead with the sanitized/redacted export you mentioned. For our test harness the minimal redaction we need is to replace full emails and credit-card PANs with fixed tokens (e.g., <EMAIL_REMOVED>, <CARD_REMOVED>) while preserving field shapes and lengths.

2) Regarding load testing: for the hosted POC environment we typically suggest a baseline of 50–100 RPS for short bursts to validate routing and batching behavior, with step-ups to 300 RPS in controlled tests if you want to evaluate autoscaling. We’ll coordinate a pre-test ramp plan so it won’t affect other tenants. Marissa — can you confirm we’ll be running batching + KV cache enabled for the session?

Also attaching a short agenda we’ll follow (POC_Agenda_20260518.pdf) and a CSV with recommended test prompts (routing_test_prompts.csv).

Thanks —
Rishi

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Morgan Blake <morgan.blake@quickcommerce.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC kickoff & hands-on session — schedule + sample payloads

Hi Morgan — quick intro: I’ll run the prompts and routing walkthrough, and steer the hands-on tests. A couple practical asks to make the session high-value:

- Please include 8–12 real-ish examples per prompt type (search, checkout, support chat). Synthetic is fine as long as it mirrors token length and typical user language.
- If you have any examples that should definitely be treated as PII (or belong to EU customers), flag them in the file with a tag field (e.g., "region": "eu") so we don’t accidentally include them in shared logs.
- For routing rules, a short mapping table (label -> criteria) is ideal.

During the session we’ll:
1) validate correctness of top N responses for each prompt set (you’ll define top N)
2) exercise routing to model variants and observe latency cost tradeoffs
3) run a 10-minute sustained load at 100 RPS + 1-minute 300 RPS spike to validate autoscale and throttling behavior

I’ve attached the CSV of test prompts and a skeleton rubric we’ll use for evaluation. If there’s anything you want added to the rubric (accuracy vs. helpfulness weighting), tell me before Friday EOD.

—Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Sam

Thanks for the update, Sam — Thu May 21, 10:30–12:00 PT works for our team. Confirming final checklist before the session:
- QuickCommerce uploads redacted sample file: quickcommerce_sample_payloads_redacted.json (we have Drive access)
- QuickCommerce to provide final 10–20 priority prompts for evaluation (CSV preferred)
- Marissa to share rubric (done) and initial routing tests CSV (done)

-Rishi
